Hi Maria —

Attaching a focused worksheet and a one-page MAP insert that defines the cost gating we normally use for pilots. High level:

- Baseline (no caching / conservative batching): measure tokens per USD and 95p latency for canonical prompts (we recommend 200–300 tokens/session for Primex).
- Cache-enabled run: enable prefix/KV caching (session-level cache TTL 24h) and re-run same workload — expect 20–45% tokens/$ improvement depending on hit-rate.
- Batching sensitivity: run at per-request concurrency targets (low: 5rps, medium: 25rps, high: 75rps) to surface latency vs unit-cost trade-offs.
- Acceptance gate: pilot passes if cost per 1M helpful tokens is <= target and 95p latency <= agreed SLO in at least two of three test windows.

I included an editable workbook (primex_map_econ_workbook_v1.xlsx) with our assumptions — please share it with procurement and legal. We suggest the MAP include these specific checkpoints and who owns the validation artifacts.

Proposed short timeline is in the attached PDF. If that looks good I can lock it into the MAP and we can add the procurement sign-off line item.

Next steps: I’ll loop in Monica (CS) to confirm the expected caching hit-rate given Primex's usage pattern; Karthik will call out any runtime constraints for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ben / Tessa / Monica —

A few concrete notes to stitch into the MAP workbook so downstream teams (SRE/procurement) have actionable checks:

- Tokens/$ baseline: we should define it as "effective helpful tokens per USD billed to customer" (i.e., exclude prompt tokens flagged as system-only in the eval). Put a sample target: 750k–1.2M helpful tokens per $1k depending on model class.
- Cache assumptions: best to present gates as ranges and a validation method. Example: if cache hit-rate >= 40% on the canonical prompt set, we assume medium-case unit-econ (apply 30% cost reduction). If < 25% hit-rate we label as low-case and require remediation. Include the exact query-matching rules we used for hit-rate calculation in the workbook appendix.
- Batching: provide recommended max batch sizes per model family and a latency SLO delta table (e.g., batching size 4 -> +10–25ms median, size 16 -> +40–120ms median depending on GPU kernel). Give test permutations: cold cache + batch=1 (baseline), warm cache + batch=8 (expected optimum), warm cache + batch=32 (high throughput stress).
- Measurement windows: 3 windows of 2 hours each across different times-of-day to catch diurnal effects; each window must produce >=2000 requests to be statistically meaningful.

I’ll add these rows to the workbook. Also agree with Ben on a one-time credit clause — suggest cap at 10% of pilot invoiced amount.

-Karthik

Hi Maria — quick CS perspective and concrete numbers after reviewing Primex sample corpus:

- Expected cache hit-rate (session-level prefix caching, 24h TTL): 42% (median) with top-10 templates representing ~60% of traffic; range across endpoints 30–55%.
- For the MAP gates I recommend:
  * Pass (green): hit-rate >= 40% and 95p latency <= 450ms under medium concurrency (25rps).
  * Conditional (amber): hit-rate 25–39% — Redwood/Primex to run a 2-week tuning sprint (prompts + caching rules) with defined delivery SLA.
  * Fail (red): hit-rate < 25% or 95p latency > 750ms at baseline.

- Cost guidance: with our baseline model family (quantized-medium), expected helpful tokens per $1k: 800k (no cache), 1.15M (with median cache), and up to 1.4M in best cases. We’ll populate the workbook with these figures by tomorrow noon.

Maria — if that aligns, I’ll add these numerics into the "MAP acceptance criteria" page and circulate a version for procurement signatures. Also happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk the procurement/legal team through the measurement methodology.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
